causal_computational_description: Existing functional structure is copied so that one copy preserves current function while the other can be modified without immediate loss. VERIFIED as structurally neutral in at least one substrate: in Lindgren's memory-m encoding the doubled string ignores the new most-significant bit, so neutrality at creation is a fact of the encoding, not an empirical observation.
required_preconditions: variable-length or growable representation; copy operator; phenotype invariant (or nearly) under the copy
transformation: genome -> genome + redundant copy; phenotype unchanged at creation (neutral)
observable_consequence: neutral period; later divergence of the copies
downstream_effect: changes the accessible mutation set: modifications of the copy that would have been lethal become viable
known_failure_modes: bloat; copies never diverge; copy cost outweighs benefit
substrate_dependence: requires a representation where a copy is executable/expressible
status: PART (causal description survives primary-source check in one substrate; downstream effect still untested)
kill_observation: Descendant mutation-effect distribution after duplication equals that of matched non-duplicated lineages. Altenberg's Theorem 4 predicts otherwise and was never measured, so this is a live, cheap test.

locators.note: Lindgren & Nordahl ECAL93 p.606, gene duplication operator and its neutrality
Altenberg 1994 Theorem 4 couples duplication to the rate of evolvability change

PRIMARY_QUOTE: 'Gene duplication is a neutral mutation, which increases the size of the evolutionary search space without immediately affecting the phenotype. Additional point mutations can then give rise to new strategies without shorter memory equivalents.' -- Lindgren & Nordahl, ECAL93 p.606
THEORETICAL_RATE_LAW: Altenberg 1994 Theorem 4: evolvability, defined as the probability that a duplicated random block of code increases fitness, increases at a rate proportional to the variance in the constructional fitnesses of its blocks -- Fisher's fundamental theorem applied to evolvability rather than fitness. NOTE: the proportionality constant nu_0/rho_t decays as the program grows, the model assumes blocks can be added but not deleted or disrupted and that constructional fitness is constant, and Altenberg states the tests were 'currently under way', i.e. this is theory awaiting measurement.

causal_computational_description: Newly introduced structural variation is shielded for a bounded time from competitive elimination by comparing it only within a compatibility class or under a relaxed criterion.
required_preconditions: a distance/compatibility measure or a non-fitness admission rule
transformation: selection pressure on novel structures is reduced for k generations
observable_consequence: more structurally diverse populations; survival of initially inferior structures
downstream_effect: structures that require several steps to become useful can be completed
known_failure_modes: protecting junk; parameter sensitivity of the compatibility threshold
kill_observation: Protection improves final fitness but not descendant acquisition rate under any evolvability measure.
NOTE_2026-09-03: Research pass did NOT check whether NEAT's component ablations used any evolvability endpoint. The fan-out reached Stanley 2002 (nn.cs.utexas.edu/downloads/papers/stanley.ec02.pdf) and the 2004 thesis (stanley.phd04.pdf) but no claim survived verification. Treat the 'fitness endpoint only' belief as STILL UNVERIFIED, not as established.

causal_computational_description: The population traverses alternative implementations of the same phenotype; the set of one-step-accessible phenotypes changes along the traverse without performance change.
required_preconditions: many-to-one genotype-phenotype map with connected neutral sets
transformation: genotype moves; phenotype constant; neighbourhood changes
observable_consequence: long stasis followed by sudden transition
downstream_effect: innovation becomes accessible from some neutral positions and not others
known_failure_modes: neutrality without connectivity; drift too slow relative to budget
minimum_reconstruction_needed: RNA flow reactor with pinned parameter set, or linear-GP phenotype network
kill_observation: Transition probability is independent of position on the neutral network.

causal_computational_description: A fitness-reducing change creates a genotype from which a high-value change is one step away, when it was several steps away before.
required_preconditions: finite population with drift or reduced purifying selection; epistasis
observable_consequence: transient fitness dip preceding a jump
downstream_effect: opens a region unreachable by strictly ascending paths
known_failure_modes: purged before use; confounded with compensatory mutation

causal_computational_description: Intermediate structures receive value from the environment before the terminal capability exists, so partial machinery is retained.
observable_consequence: terminal capability appears only when intermediates are rewarded (ablation)

causal_computational_description: An acquired structure or a coupled second population alters the selection environment so that previously neutral structures acquire value.
required_preconditions: environment or opponent is itself variable and coupled to the population
transformation: selection gradient changes as a function of population state
observable_consequence: sequences of capabilities unreachable under fixed environment
evidence_strength: perturbation (POET vs direct optimisation; Avida parasites; verify)
kill_observation: Matched-compute curriculum baseline reaches the same regions.

causal_computational_description: A structure selected in context A is copied into context B where it solves a problem it was not selected for.
required_preconditions: multiple simultaneous contexts and a copy channel
transformation: context-B search starts from an A-derived point
kill_observation: Transfer contributes nothing beyond extra evaluations.

causal_computational_description: At high mutation rates, lineages whose structure reduces the phenotypic effect of mutations outcompete fitter but fragile lineages; the structure changes which mutations are neutral.
required_preconditions: mutation rate high enough that offspring viability matters
transformation: selection acts on the distribution of offspring effects, not just parent fitness
observable_consequence: fitter lineage loses; neutral code accumulates
downstream_effect: altered mutation tolerance -> altered accessible set
known_failure_modes: pure bloat with no evolvability gain
kill_observation: Robust lineages are not more evolvable under environment change.

causal_computational_description: Within-lifetime adaptation converts a needle-in-haystack fitness function into a graded one, changing the direction and magnitude of selection on the heritable part.
required_preconditions: plastic component with cost; heritable component
observable_consequence: faster acquisition, then assimilation and loss of plasticity
known_failure_modes: cost of learning too high; assimilation removes future flexibility

causal_computational_description: Information is carried by localized boundaries between regular regions; their collisions implement conditional transformations, giving a distributed system the equivalent of signals and gates.
required_preconditions: regular domains that can coexist; boundary propagation
downstream_effect: a representation change that makes further strategies composable
known_failure_modes: rare to discover; brittle to lattice size
kill_observation: Particle strategies confer no advantage in subsequent tasks (no composability).

causal_computational_description: Search sits in a metastable region until a rare structural change opens a new region; time-in-epoch is a measurable acquisition cost.
required_preconditions: neutral or near-neutral plateau; rare transition
transformation: none until transition; then a step in reachable set
known_failure_modes: epochs that are pure drift with no structural change
kill_observation: Epoch boundaries do not coincide with any structural change in the elite lineage.

causal_computational_description: A substructure is invoked from multiple sites so one mutation changes many phenotypic loci coherently.
transformation: one genotypic change -> coordinated phenotypic change
observable_consequence: regularity; reduced genome size for a given function
downstream_effect: changes the mutation-effect distribution toward coordinated variation
minimum_reconstruction_needed: GP with/without ADFs on a multi-part task
kill_observation: Module reuse does not change time-to-adaptation after environment shift.

causal_computational_description: Structures carry an origin identifier so recombination aligns homologous parts regardless of current position.
kill_observation: No effect without recombination (then it is not a part, it is a crossover repair).

causal_computational_description: Limited interaction range slows competitive exclusion so alternative implementations coexist longer.
downstream_effect: more starting points for later innovation
kill_observation: Diversity gain does not translate to reachability gain.

causal_computational_description: When a prediction fails reliably, the system introduces a new internal state variable to explain the failure, expanding its representation.
required_preconditions: prediction, failure detection, ability to add state
transformation: representation grows in response to a failure class
downstream_effect: reachability of behaviours requiring hidden state

causal_computational_description: The variation operator is itself part of the heritable structure and evolves.
required_preconditions: representation that can express its own copy/mutate procedure
observable_consequence: divergent per-lineage mutation spectra; frequent collapse
kill_observation: Evolved operators never beat a fixed operator on downstream acquisition.

causal_computational_description: Search recruits an unmodelled property of the substrate or environment as a computational resource.
required_preconditions: physics richer than the designer's model
transformation: problem solved by a channel outside the intended representation
observable_consequence: solutions that fail when the channel is removed
downstream_effect: reachability depends on hidden resources; also a detector failure mode
kill_observation: N/A (used as negative control for detectors).

causal_computational_description: The map from genotype to phenotype biases which phenotypes are reachable independent of selection; frequent phenotypes are found first regardless of fitness.
transformation: search distribution over phenotypes is set by map bias
observable_consequence: arrival order predicted by phenotype frequency
downstream_effect: reachability ceiling that selection cannot lift
minimum_reconstruction_needed: phenotype network enumeration on a small map

causal_computational_description: The distribution of one-step offspring phenotypes is measured directly and used as the selection criterion, so search optimises reachable-region size rather than task performance.
required_preconditions: ability to generate and evaluate throwaway offspring; a behavioural distance measure
transformation: fitness(individual) := count of behaviourally distinct offspring above a threshold
observable_consequence: populations whose offspring clouds cover more of an unseen environment
downstream_effect: reachable-region size in a transfer context (measured, p<0.001 vs novelty and objective search)
replication_status: reported; measure inherited from Lehman & Stanley 2011/2013 and Velez & Clune 2014
known_failure_modes: scalar threshold count is not the full mutational-effect distribution; union over 200 offspring inflates coverage if one wanders far; one mutation step only; snapshot not change
kill_observation: N/A -- this part exists to hold the seat accountable: the field already does this.
